argument:
Solarvest's RM2.371bn unbilled order book creates a concrete revenue-conversion opportunity, complemented by electricity-sales growth of 25.8%. Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, profit 19.8%, and net margin improved from 11.5% to 12.2%. These observations support the case that delivered projects and recurring electricity activity can build earnings beyond a single headline.

The order book is not cash, and 89.1% EPCC exposure makes timing and execution central. Sequential revenue fell from RM270.5m, while debt and FCF remain unknown. Stable domestic policy is useful financing context, not a verified subsidy catalyst. The intact uptrend supports interest, but RSI above 82 and weak volume mean a bullish long-term scenario does not establish an attractive immediate entry.
key_points: Profit outgrew revenue and reported margin improved.
Order book and electricity sales offer different potential growth channels.
EPCC conversion, funding and overbought pricing remain the key hurdles.
